description_full: Hansoh Pharmaceutical Group Company Limited, an investment holding company, engages in the research, development, production, and sale of pharmaceutical products in the People's Republic of China. The company provides products for therapeutic areas, including anti-infection, central nervous system, oncology, and metabolic and other diseases, as well as autoimmune diseases. Its principal products include Ameile, Hansoh Xinfu, Pulaile, Xintai, Xinmei, Gainuo, Tanneng, and Pulaitan; Hengmu, Hengsen, Oulanning, Ailanning, and Ameining; XINYUE; and Saint Luolai, Fulaimei, Ruibote, Fulaidi, Punuoan tablets, etc. It has licence agreements with GlaxoSmithKline Intellectual Property (No.4) Limited to develop, manufacture, and commercialize HS-20089 and HS-20093 for the treatment of patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) with disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy; Biotheus Inc. to develop, produce, and commercialize bispecific antibody-drug conjugate product; and Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC (MSD) to develop, manufacture, and commercialize HS-10535, an investigational pre-clinical oral small molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, as well as a strategic collaboration with F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd for developing antibody-drug conjugate programs. The company was founded in 1995 and is headquartered in Shanghai, China. Hansoh Pharmaceutical Group Company Limited operates as a subsidiary of Stellar Infinity Company Ltd.

financial_summary: Hansoh Pharmaceutical Group Co  is a large-cap healthcare business with a $24.7B market cap on $2.3B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +14% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +2.4pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 58% against a 8% cost of capital — a 50-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 90% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $938M in free cash flow — roughly 42 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.21× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Net dilution runs at 1.0% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 80% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 4.2× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
